detail.body:
## Description

This PR modifies FSDP engine for efficient loading of large dense models, such as Qwen3-VL-32B, to avoid out-of-memory error when initializing the model. Moreover, it provides an example of how VLLM environment variables should be set properly so that tensor parallelism can be applied successfully using VLLM on Ascned NPUs.

## Type of Change

<!-- Mark the relevant option with an 'x' -->

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not
  work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Code refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Test coverage improvement

## Checklist

<!-- Mark with 'x' what you've done -->

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guide](../CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [ ] I have run formatting tools (pre-commit or manual)
- [ ] I have run relevant unit tests and they pass
- [ ] I have added tests for new functionality
- [ ] I have updated documentation if needed
- [ ] My branch is up to date with main
- [ ] This PR introduces breaking changes (if yes, fill out details below)
- [ ] If this PR changes documentation, I have built and previewed it locally with
  `jb build docs`
- [ ] No critical issues raised by AI reviewers (`/gemini review`)

+gconfig:
+  n_samples: 4
+  min_new_tokens: 0

+  greedy: false
+  temperature: 1.0
+
+actor:
+  experiment_name: ${experiment_name}
+  trial_name: ${trial_name}
+  path: Qwen/Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct
+  init_from_scratch: false
+  disable_dropout: true
+  gradient_checkpointing: true
+  dtype: bfloat16
+  mb_spec:
+    max_tokens_per_mb: 2048
+  optimizer:
+    type: adam
+    lr: 2e-6
+    weight_decay: 0.01
+    beta1: 0.9
+    beta2: 0.999
+    eps: 1e-8
+    lr_scheduler_type: constant
+    gradient_clipping: 1.0
+    warmup_steps_proportion: 0.001
+  eps_clip: 0.4
+  temperature: ${gconfig.temperature}
+  reward_scaling: 10.0
+  reward_bias: -0.5
+  kl_ctl: 0.0
+  ppo_n_minibatches: 1
+  recompute_logprob: true
+  use_decoupled_loss: true
+  behav_imp_weight_cap: 5.0
+  reward_norm:
+    mean_level: group
+    std_level: group
+    group_size: ${gconfig.n_samples}
+  adv_norm:
+    mean_level: batch
+    std_level: batch
+  max_new_tokens: ${gconfig.max_new_tokens}
+  scheduling_spec:
+    - task_type: worker
+      port_count: 2
+      gpu: 1
+      cpu: 4
+      mem: 32
+      cmd: python3 -m areal.infra.rpc.rpc_server
+      env_vars: {}
+  fsdp:
+    memory_efficient_load: true
+
+ref:
+  experiment_name: ${experiment_name}
+  trial_name: ${trial_name}
+  path: ${actor.path}
+  init_from_scratch: false
+  disable_dropout: true
+  dtype: ${actor.dtype}
+  mb_spec:
+    max_tokens_per_mb: 2048
+  optimizer: null
+  scheduling_strategy:
+    type: colocation
+    target: actor
+  scheduling_spec: ${actor.scheduling_spec}
+
+# SGLang
+sglang:
+  model_path: ${actor.path}
+  random_seed: ${seed}
+  skip_tokenizer_init: true
+  dtype: ${actor.dtype}
+  max_running_requests: 64
+  context_length: 32768
+  mem_fraction_static: 0.8
+  enable_multimodal: true
+
+vllm:
+  model: ${actor.path}
+  seed: ${seed}
+  skip_tokenizer_init: false
+  dtype: ${actor.dtype}
+  max_model_len: 32768
+  gpu_memory_utilization: 0.9
+  disable_sliding_window: false
+
+
+# datasets
+train_dataset:
+  batch_size: 32
+  shuffle: true
+  pin_memory: true
+  num_workers: 4
+  path: hiyouga/geometry3k
+  type: rl
+
+valid_dataset:
+  batch_size: 32
+  pin_memory: true
+  num_workers: 4
+  path: hiyouga/geometry3k
+  type: rl
+
+# Utilities
+saver:
+  experiment_name: ${experiment_name}
+  trial_name: ${trial_name}
+  fileroot: ${cluster.fileroot}
+  freq_epochs: 1
+  freq_steps: null
+  freq_secs: null
+
+recover:
+  mode: disabled
+  experiment_name: ${experiment_name}
+  trial_name: ${trial_name}
+  fileroot: ${cluster.fileroot}
+  freq_epochs: 1
+  freq_steps: null
+  freq_secs: 3600
+
+evaluator:
+  experiment_name: ${experiment_name}
+  trial_name: ${trial_name}
+  fileroot: ${cluster.fileroot}
+  freq_epochs: 1
+  freq_steps: null
+  freq_secs: null
+
+stats_logger:
+  experiment_name: ${experiment_name}
+  trial_name: ${trial_name}
+  fileroot: ${cluster.fileroot}
+  wandb:
+    mode: disabled
+
+perf_tracer:
+  experiment_name: ${experiment_name}
+  trial_name: ${trial_name}
+  fileroot: ${cluster.fileroot}
+  enabled: false
+  session_tracer:
+    enabled: false

![security-high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/security-high-priority.svg) ![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The call to `get_state_dict_from_repo_id_or_path` on line 297 introduces a potential insecure deserialization vulnerability. This utility function (defined in `areal/utils/save_load.py`) uses `torch.load` to process `.bin` files without setting `weights_only=True`. Since `torch.load` uses the `pickle` module internally, it is susceptible to arbitrary code execution if a malicious model checkpoint is loaded. An attacker who can influence the `self.config.path` (e.g., via CLI overrides) could achieve remote code execution (RCE). It is recommended to update the utility function to use `weights_only=True` or prefer the `safetensors` format for loading weights.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

For better script robustness, it's recommended to add `set -e` at the beginning of the script. This will cause the script to exit immediately if a command exits with a non-zero status, preventing unexpected behavior from subsequent commands.

```suggestion
set -e
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `allocation_mode` `vllm:d4p1t1+d4p1t1` appears to be syntactically incorrect, as the part after `+` should specify a role (e.g., `fsdp`). Assuming it's a typo for a two-role allocation, it would allocate 8 GPUs in total (4 for each role), which contradicts `n_gpus_per_node: 16` on line 11. The value from the accompanying shell script, `vllm:d1t8+fsdp:d1t8`, is consistent with 16 GPUs and seems more appropriate. To avoid confusion and potential errors, it's best to correct this in the YAML file.

```yaml
allocation_mode: vllm:d1t8+fsdp:d1t8
```

This pull request introduces significant enhancements for handling large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) within the FSDP engine, particularly focusing on memory efficiency during model initialization. It enables a new memory-efficient loading strategy that mitigates out-of-memory errors for models like Qwen3-VL-32B by offloading initial weight loading to the CPU. Additionally, it provides a concrete example demonstrating how to configure VLLM for tensor parallelism on Ascend NPUs, ensuring successful deployment and training of these large models. ### Highlights * **Memory-Efficient Model Loading**: Introduced a new `memory_efficient_load` configuration option for FSDP, allowing model weights to be initialized on CPU to reduce peak GPU memory during loading, especially for large models. For VLMs, each rank loads weights independently on CPU. * **FSDP Engine Enhancements**: Implemented the memory-efficient loading mechanism within the FSDP engine, where rank 0 loads pretrained weights (or each rank loads independently for VLMs) and broadcasts them after sharding. ## Code Review

This pull request introduces a `memory_efficient_load` option for FSDP to reduce peak GPU memory usage during model initialization, which is particularly useful for large models. The core logic involves creating the model on the CPU, loading weights on rank 0, and then broadcasting them. A critical security vulnerability has been identified: the use of `torch.load` without `weights_only=True` in the underlying weight-loading logic can lead to arbitrary code execution if a malicious checkpoint is provided. It is strongly recommended to update the weight-loading utilities to use `weights_only=True` or prefer the `safetensors` format to mitigate this risk. Additionally, minor issues were found in the new example files related to script robustness and configuration consistency.
